newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr slightly firmer vs yen but top-heavy in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr slightly firmer vs yen but top-heavy in Tokyo.

text.p: 0125 GMT --*Dollar up slightly against yen in morning Tokyo after earlier edging up on purchases by some trust banks and commercial buying at Japan's local fixing at 0100 GMT.
*But greenback's topside remains heavy near 116.30 and up with exporter offers.
*Traders expect activity to stay quiet ahead of U.S. trade data and long weekend in Japan.
*A city bank dealer said a jump to 117 yen was possible if greenback absorbs heavy offers near 116.40 yen, but he expected no trading energy or incentives in Tokyo to test upside.
*Earlier, light technical purchases detected in mark/yen. Mark stood near 64.74/77 yen at 0137 GMT against 64.68 yen in late New York on Thursday.
*"Some exporters are placing offers near 116.20-30 yen and heavy offers are lined up especially near 116.70 yen, so it is difficult to test the dollar upside," a city bank dealer said.
*U.S. international trade data for May due at 1230 GMT. Experts surveyed by Reuters call for modest up-tick in trade gap to $9.18 billion from $8.36 billion in April.
*Tokyo operators expect trade data to have limited impact unless it deviates sharply from expectations.
*Dollar steady against yen in early Tokyo trade, but upside seen capped around 116.30 yen by offers from Japanese exporters and life insurers.
*Dollar/yen downside also seen limited due to bargain-hunting interest from institutional investors.
*Some Japanese investors are still keen to buy dollars to unwind hedges, traders said.
*Japanese financial markets will be closed on Monday for national holiday.
